items.title: NEW — `lazy` PARAMETERS and `lazy` MODULE BINDINGS (the RATIFIED 2026-07-21 paper `lazy.md`; the owner's 'late' bindings — `late` is the spelling the paper rejected for naming Dart's different assign-before-use contract): S1 lazy parameters — `fun expect(self, lazy message: str)`: the argument is THUNKED at the call site, forced on the parameter's first read, memoized (call-by-need: at most once, late; never read → never runs), forwarded thunk-to-thunk, v1 rejections with steers (resource, async and context-reading arguments), an arity/laziness agreement check for impls of lazy-parameter signatures, `__force` + its interpreter arm; S2 lazy module bindings — `lazy let database: Database = Database::open("kolt.db");`: the initializer runs at FIRST USE then memoizes, cycle trap ('lazy initialization cycle: `database`'), a failed initializer POISONS the binding, resources loan-only/write-frozen as today, platform coloring from the initializer, sync and context-free. UNBLOCKED at the owner's call 2026-09-14: the paper's slices were 'sequenced at the user's call' and NEVER ENTERED THE TRACKER (its 'F5/F7' slots were the pre-tracker backlog's; no item open or closed carries it; probed on 9b22ec36: `lazy` is not a keyword — `lazy let` and `lazy fallback` fail as unknown names). One shape lowers both positions: a memo cell `{ state, value, thunk }` with `__force` (pending → running → done \| poisoned; `running` is the cycle trap)
items.discussion: the owner (2026-09-14): 'unblock `late` bindings (I believe they are already filed) for both globals and parameters' — they were not filed; filed now, READY, no ruling owed (the paper's §6 calls stand: poison, `lazy`, retrofit gated). S3 — std adoption + the `unwrap_or`/`expect` → `lazy fallback` retrofit sweep, gated on the corpus/std/docs differential (§6b) — is its own item once S1/S2 land
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-09-14, READY (paper ratified; owner unblocked)
items.body: S1 (lazy.md §1, §5): keyword `lazy` through lexer/parser/formatter and the THREE homes (lexer, TextMate grammar, book theme — AGENTS.md invariant, same commit); the parameter modifier in the three grammar homes (free fn, method, trait signature); call-site thunking (a closure over the free variables — every existing capture rule applies: a view capture is rejected, a resource local is an R9 capture); forcing on first read inside the callee, memoized; forwarding to a lazy position passes the cell, to an eager position forces; rejections: resource argument ('resources stay eager'), awaiting argument (steer: `async expr` → pass the `Task`), context-reading argument (steer: pass a closure); impls of a lazy-parameter signature must agree in laziness (targeted check, not waiting on B29); hover renders `lazy`. Pins: forced-once (counting side effect), never-forced-never-runs, forwarding chains, each rejection, trait mismatch, hover, interpreter parity for `__force`. S2 (§2): the memo cell at module scope; first-use init order observable via prints; cycle trap; poison (re-panic on later touches with the poisoned message); loan-only/write-frozen inheritance for resources with a real `Database` pin; platform coloring of the initializer; docs — spec §6.x sentence for bindings, std pages for `expect`/`unwrap_or`, tour 'lazy resources' section (the eager idiom stays primary). Exclusions stand (§3): no lazy local `let`, no lazy fields, no lazy resource parameters. Ledger rows for every new refusal. Lane: lang; two slices, S1 first (derisks the memo lowering).

items.title: NEW — CALL-OPERATOR OVERLOADING: `impl MyStruct with Callable { fun call(self, n: f64): f64 { .. } }` makes a struct VALUE callable — `let scale = Scale::new(0.25); scale(2f)` lowers to `scale.call(2f)`. Today `my_struct(2f)` is refused ('cannot call this as a function: it is MyStruct', `not_callable_message` analyzer.rs:36289) and `Callable` does not exist ('cannot find trait `Callable`'); kolt's `src/lib/scale_step.vl` carries the use case with a FIXME (`Scale { unit }` + `fun get(self, n: f64): Length { Length::rem(self.unit * n) }` — 'Make into call operator overload when supported'). Shape: `Callable` is a MARKER trait in `std::operators` beside `Add`/`Sub`/`Lift` — `trait Callable {}` — and the `call` method the impl declares carries the ARITY and types (no variadic generics needed: the analyzer resolves `x(args)` on a receiver whose type implements `Callable` exactly as it resolves `x.call(args)`, so the signature check is the ordinary method check). A `Callable` value is plain DATA, so `const let space = Scale::new(0.25);` is a const result TODAY under G24's data rule and `space(2f)` in a const context calls through the interpreter — the scale use case needs no closure snapshot
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-14) with the sketch `impl MyStruct with Callable { fun call(PARAMETERS) { .. } }` / `let value = my_struct();`. OWNER QUESTIONS: (Q1) a `Callable` value in a CLOSURE-typed position — does `let f: \|f64\| Length = scale;` coerce (fn-coercion.md §1's set gains 'a value whose type implements `Callable`', lowered to `\|n\| scale.call(n)`)? rec: yes, in the same slice — it is what lets a `Callable` stand where a closure parameter is expected (`list.map(scale)`); (Q2) a field holding a `Callable`: `a.b(c)` stays METHOD resolution (today's meaning); the field call is spelled `(a.b)(c)` — Rust's rule; rec: adopt, with a steer when `b` is a `Callable` field and no method `b` exists
items.body: std: `trait Callable {}` in operators.vl with the doc contract (a `call` method of the impl's own arity; `self` by value like every method). Analyzer: in the call-subject arm, before `not_callable_message`, when the subject's type implements `Callable` resolve the call as the method `call` on it (argument checking, generics, context clauses — all the method path's); refuse `impl T with Callable` that declares no `call` (curated row: 'implementing `Callable` requires a `call` method'); a type with a `call` method but no `Callable` impl keeps today's refusal plus the steer 'implement `Callable` to call it as a function'; a struct TYPE name called (`Point(1, 2)`) keeps its own refusal (analyzer.rs:37211). Transformer: `x(args)` → `x.call(args)` (a struct is a plain JS object, so the name is free); interpreter arm for const contexts. Q1 coercion: fn-coercion rule extended, lowered as a wrapping closure; Q2 field rule + steer. Formatter/TextMate: nothing (ordinary call syntax). Pins: the call resolves and type-checks like the method (wrong arity/type errors at the call site name `call`); a `Callable` with a context clause on `call` inherits it at the call; `const` interpreter parity; kolt scale_step.vl rewritten to `impl Scale with Callable { fun call(self, n: f64): Length }` at the owner's word; Q1/Q2 pins. Ledger rows: the two new refusals + the steer. Cross-links: G24 (closure results — this item covers the data-shaped callable; G24 the genuine closure), method-resolution.md, fn-coercion.md.
